summary.title: What file do I need?
summary.saints: A saints list: each saint with a unique id, name, dates, country and their characteristics (the bullet points).
summary.collections: Optional: collections to group them. If a collection already exists, its new saints are added to it.
summary.existing: Saints whose id is already in your library are skipped; nothing is overwritten unless you choose another mode.

format.tip: Tip: “Export JSON” in Settings writes your current library in this same format; you can use it as a model.

top.source: Where the data comes from: document, notes, factCheckedIndividually.
top.collections: Optional collections that group saints by id.

saint.id: Unique, stable identifier, lowercase with hyphens: “santa-rosa-de-lima”. If it already exists in your library, the saint is skipped (default mode).
saint.name: Name as printed.
saint.birthYear: Birth year; null if unknown. Don't make up dates.
saint.ageAtDeath: Age at death; null if unknown.
saint.portraitPath: Leave it as null. Photos are uploaded later with “Import portraits”.
saint.categories: Tags for filtering: santos-jovenes, martires, educadores-y-guias, patronos-de-la-juventud… Can be empty [].
saint.canonizationYear: Canonization year; null if it doesn't apply or is unknown.
saint.characteristics: The worksheet's bullet points, in order (5–8 recommended). See below.
saint.sources: Sources or links for review. Can be empty [].

characteristic.text: The bullet point. Can't be empty. For miracles keep “según testimonios”, “se le atribuye”…
characteristic.type: biography, virtue, miracle, patronage, martyrdom, canonization, legacy or other.

collection.id: Unique identifier. If it already exists, its new saints are added to that collection.
collection.name: Visible name.
collection.saintIds: Saint ids in order. They can be from the file or already in your library.
